# Command reference

Every `datarepo` command, with every argument it takes. This page is generated from the program's own help, so it lists exactly what the executable accepts; `datarepo <command> -h` prints the same text.

New here? Start with [getting-started.md](getting-started.md), which runs the main commands end to end on the example instance shipped in this repository.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`doctor`](#datarepo-doctor) | report this build's version, schema and components, and any registered MCP servers |
| [`manifest`](#datarepo-manifest) | show what the producing instance offers, and check its run_enrichment maps |
| [`ingest`](#datarepo-ingest) | build a Parquet bundle for one or more datasets |
| [`inspect`](#datarepo-inspect) | summarise a written bundle |
| [`study`](#datarepo-study) | write a study layer's delivered rows as a study bundle |
| [`run`](#datarepo-run) | run a released engine on stored data (the instance operator's step) |
| [`publish`](#datarepo-publish) | build the catalog from every ingested dataset, then write the static site |
| [`build`](#datarepo-build) | load bundles into one DuckDB catalog |
| [`site`](#datarepo-site) | write the public static site for one catalog |
| [`catalog`](#datarepo-catalog) | summarise a built catalog |
| [`query`](#datarepo-query) | run one read-only SQL query against a catalog |
| [`mcp`](#datarepo-mcp) | serve one catalog to an agent over stdio (MCP) |

`datarepo --version` prints the version. A release build says its version (`datarepo 1.0.0`); a build from source says `0.0.0-dev`.

**Exit status.** `0` when the command did what it was asked, including a no-op it reports (an unchanged bundle or catalog, a delivery already written). `1` when it refused: a dataset the manifest excludes, a check that failed, a file that does not match its record. The reason is on standard error. `2` for a command line it cannot parse.

## Check the machine

Run first on a new machine.

### `datarepo doctor`

Report this build's version, schema and components, and any registered MCP servers.

```text
usage: datarepo doctor [-h]

report this build's version, schema and components, and any registered MCP servers

options:
  -h, --help             show this help message and exit
```

## Ingest: a producer's run becomes a bundle

An instance operator runs these once per dataset, after the search. See [ingest.md](ingest.md) and [study.md](study.md).

### `datarepo manifest`

Show what the producing instance offers, and check its run_enrichment maps.

```text
usage: datarepo manifest [-h] manifest

show what the producing instance offers, and check its run_enrichment maps

positional arguments:
  manifest               the producing instance's manifest.yaml

options:
  -h, --help             show this help message and exit
```

A dataset with a `run_enrichment` map is checked the way `ingest` would check it, against the run folder when it is reachable. A map `ingest` would refuse is printed as `REFUSED` and the command exits `1`, so a wrong map is found before a re-ingest.

### `datarepo ingest`

Build a Parquet bundle for one or more datasets.

```text
usage: datarepo ingest [-h] [--store STORE] [--mm-settings MM_SETTINGS] [--overwrite] [-v] [--json] manifest [accession ...]

build a Parquet bundle for one or more datasets

positional arguments:
  manifest               the producing instance's manifest.yaml
  accession              datasets to ingest; default is every 'include' (zero or more)

options:
  -h, --help             show this help message and exit
  --store STORE          where to write bundles; default is the manifest's store
  --mm-settings MM_SETTINGS
                         MetaMorpheus install to read modification definitions from
  --overwrite            rebuild a bundle that already exists
  -v, --verbose          show every reconciliation check
  --json                 print one JSON envelope on stdout; the human report goes to stderr
```

With `--json`, standard output carries exactly one JSON object and nothing else; the human report goes to standard error. Its keys: `datarepo` (the version), `ok`, `exit_code`, `reasons`, and `datasets`, one per accession, each with `accession`, `status` (`ingested`, `unchanged`, `excluded`, `refused` or `error`) and `reasons`, plus for a written bundle `bundle_id`, `bundle_path`, `tables` (row counts), `checks`, `mismatches`, `unresolved_modifications`, `unmatched_runs` and `findings` (the open warning codes).

### `datarepo inspect`

Summarise a written bundle.

```text
usage: datarepo inspect [-h] [--json] bundle

summarise a written bundle

positional arguments:
  bundle                 bundle directory or its bundle.json

options:
  -h, --help             show this help message and exit
  --json                 print the manifest verbatim
```

### `datarepo study`

Write a study layer's delivered rows as a study bundle.

```text
usage: datarepo study [-h] [--store STORE] [--overwrite] manifest

write a study layer's delivered rows as a study bundle

positional arguments:
  manifest               the study delivery's study.yaml

options:
  -h, --help             show this help message and exit
  --store STORE          where to write the bundle; default is the manifest's store
  --overwrite            rewrite a delivery already written
```

### `datarepo run`

Run a released engine on stored data (the instance operator's step).

```text
usage: datarepo run [-h] --store STORE [--input ROLE=PATH] [--bundle PXD=ID] [--latest] engine accession [accession ...]

run a released engine on stored data (the instance operator's step)

positional arguments:
  engine                 the engine to run: logs.resolve_genes
  accession              datasets whose searched databases to run on (one or more)

options:
  -h, --help             show this help message and exit
  --store STORE          the instance's bundle store (required)
  --input ROLE=PATH      an input file by role; repeatable
  --bundle PXD=ID        pin a dataset to one bundle id (repeatable)
  --latest               take each dataset's newest bundle
```

A development build (version `0.0.0-dev`, or no recorded commit) is refused: see [operating.md](operating.md#1-install-one-released-version).

## Build and publish: bundles become a catalog and a site

`publish` is `build` then `site` in one step. See [build.md](build.md), [site.md](site.md) and [operating.md](operating.md).

### `datarepo publish`

Build the catalog from every ingested dataset, then write the static site.

```text
usage: datarepo publish [-h] --site SITE [--store STORE] [--out OUT] [--study-latest LAYER] [--title TITLE] [--base-url BASE_URL] [--data-url DATA_URL] [--notice NOTICE] [--about ABOUT] [--purpose TEXT] [--keyword WORD] manifest [accession ...]

build the catalog from every ingested dataset, then write the static site

positional arguments:
  manifest               the producing instance's manifest.yaml
  accession              datasets to load; default is every 'include' that has a bundle, naming those without (zero or more)

options:
  -h, --help             show this help message and exit
  --site SITE            the site directory: empty, or a site written before (required)
  --store STORE          where bundles live; default is the manifest's store
  --out OUT              catalog file to write; default is <store>/../catalog.duckdb
  --study-latest LAYER   load a study layer's newest delivery; repeatable. None is loaded unless named
  --title TITLE          the site's name; default from the catalog's instance
  --base-url BASE_URL    where the site will be served, for absolute links and the sitemap
  --data-url DATA_URL    where the bundle store is served; enables downloads and croissant.json
  --notice NOTICE        a banner for the top of every page and of llms.txt
  --about ABOUT          a Markdown file: the front page's overview of the project
  --purpose TEXT         the question this instance serves
  --keyword WORD         a schema.org keyword for every dataset page; repeatable
```

### `datarepo build`

Load bundles into one DuckDB catalog.

```text
usage: datarepo build [-h] [--store STORE] [--out OUT] [--bundle PXD=ID] [--latest] [--study LAYER=ID] [--study-latest LAYER] [--release RELEASE] [--overwrite] [-v] manifest [accession ...]

load bundles into one DuckDB catalog

positional arguments:
  manifest               the producing instance's manifest.yaml
  accession              datasets to load; default is every 'include' (zero or more)

options:
  -h, --help             show this help message and exit
  --store STORE          where bundles live; default is the manifest's store
  --out OUT              catalog file to write; default is <store>/../catalog.duckdb
  --bundle PXD=ID        pin a dataset to one bundle id; repeatable
  --latest               when a dataset has several bundles, take the newest instead of refusing
  --study LAYER=ID       load a study layer's delivery, pinned to one bundle id; repeatable
  --study-latest LAYER   load a study layer's newest delivery; repeatable, refused with --release
  --release RELEASE      release version this catalog is for; requires every dataset pinned with --bundle
  --overwrite            rebuild a catalog that is current
  -v, --verbose          list every check that ran
```

### `datarepo site`

Write the public static site for one catalog.

```text
usage: datarepo site [-h] --out OUT [--title TITLE] [--base-url BASE_URL] [--data-url DATA_URL]
                     [--notice NOTICE] [--about ABOUT] [--purpose TEXT] [--keyword WORD]
                     catalog

write the public static site for one catalog

positional arguments:
  catalog                the catalog .duckdb file

options:
  -h, --help             show this help message and exit
  --out OUT              an empty directory, or a site written before (required)
  --title TITLE          the site's name; default from the catalog's instance
  --base-url BASE_URL    where the site will be served, for absolute links and the sitemap
  --data-url DATA_URL    where the bundle store is served; enables downloads and croissant.json
  --notice NOTICE        a banner for the top of every page and of llms.txt
  --about ABOUT          a Markdown file: the front page's overview of the project
  --purpose TEXT         the question this instance serves, ending "for questions about ..."; e.g. "how organelle proteomes change with age". Without it no page claims one
  --keyword WORD         a schema.org keyword for every dataset page, e.g. aging; repeatable
```

### `datarepo catalog`

Summarise a built catalog.

```text
usage: datarepo catalog [-h] [--json] catalog

summarise a built catalog

positional arguments:
  catalog                the catalog .duckdb file

options:
  -h, --help             show this help message and exit
  --json                 print the catalog's own tables verbatim
```

## Ask: read a catalog

See [querying.md](querying.md) and [mcp.md](mcp.md).

### `datarepo query`

Run one read-only SQL query against a catalog.

```text
usage: datarepo query [-h] [--format {table,tsv,json}] [--limit LIMIT] catalog sql

run one read-only SQL query against a catalog

positional arguments:
  catalog                the catalog .duckdb file
  sql                    the statement to run

options:
  -h, --help             show this help message and exit
  --format {table,tsv,json}
                         how to print the rows (default: table)
  --limit LIMIT          row cap; 0 for no cap (default: 50)
```

### `datarepo mcp`

Serve one catalog to an agent over stdio (MCP).

```text
usage: datarepo mcp [-h] [--catalog CATALOG] [--install] [--list] [--check]
                    [--name NAME] [--config CONFIG] [--force]

serve one catalog to an agent over stdio (MCP)

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --catalog CATALOG  the catalog .duckdb file to serve; never auto-discovered
  --install          register it with Claude Code and exit
  --list             show the datarepo servers already registered
  --check            open the catalog and report, without serving
  --name NAME        server name, for registering several catalogs
  --config CONFIG    MCP config to write; default is the Claude Code user
                     config
  --force            repoint an entry of that name at this catalog
```
